findings.issue: The SPEC-09 IMPORT regex only matches `import ... from '...';` statements. It does not see side-effect imports (`import '../engine/x';`) or re-exports (`export { applyAction } from '../engine/hand';`), so a later bot file could pull runtime engine code through either form and the test would still pass.
findings.evidence: const IMPORT = /^import\s+(type\s+)?([\s\S]*?)\s+from\s+'([^']+)';/gm; there is no case for `export ... from` or a bare `import '...'`. The SPEC-11 grep `from '[^.]` catches only bare-package specifiers, not relative engine paths.
findings.fix: Extend the regex to `^(?:import|export)\s+(type\s+)?(?:([\s\S]*?)\s+from\s+)?'([^']+)';` and treat a missing clause as a runtime import (a problem when it targets src/engine). Add one probe line of each form to the probe block. Or leave it as is until the TASK-6.21 lint rule replaces this test (already a listed follow-up).

findings.issue: `const hero: PublicPlayer | undefined = ...` repeats the type `find` already infers. Its only effect is to keep the `PublicPlayer` type import in use.
findings.evidence: view.players is readonly PublicPlayer[], so .find already returns PublicPlayer | undefined.
findings.fix: Drop the annotation and the PublicPlayer import, or keep both if the D-5 import list is meant to be literal.

summary: decideTag always returns recommend(view, ...).move. The D-2 shortcut fires only on flop/turn/river when currentBet - streetContribution === 0, which is the same `owed` formula and `owed === 0` test that recommendPostflop uses for check-free, so whenever the stand-in is used the move is the legal `check`. I could not build a view where the move differs. The not-to-act RangeError and the missing-check Error are raised the same way, and the stand-in never throws. The only observable difference is that a real computeEquity error on a free check would be hidden, and that cannot happen for well-formed views. Removing the street guard would be harmless too, because preflop never reads equity. defaultPolicyFactory returns TAG only at size 6, and seams.makePolicy still overrides it at every size. The A-4 edits are behaviour-neutral: no field initializer reads this.c, and the constructor assigns it first. A scratch copy ran the advice tests and vite build cleanly. src/bots imports only types from the engine. Mutants run in a scratch copy outside the repo, since deleted: (1) decideTag ignoring options was killed by SPEC-07; (2) the postflop shortcut calling recommendPostflop directly, bypassing the recommend module, was killed by SPEC-06, so the vi.mock spy really sees the calls; (3) a 6-max default with seat 1 random and the rest TAG was killed by SPEC-05's byte-identical CLI comparison; (4) playHand ignoring makePolicy at size 6 was killed by SPEC-10. Changed lines are 647 against a budget of 600; the gate warns but does not fail, and most of the overage is tests. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
